ex: We danced a tango at my sister's wedding.
The tango comes from Argentina and Uruguay.
I want to take tango lessons this year.
Can you teach me to dance the tango?
Stalking is a serious crime in many countries.
She told the police about the stalking.
Online stalking can make people feel very unsafe.
If someone is stalking you, call the police.
The casting for the new movie starts on Monday.
She went to a casting for a TV commercial.
Hundreds of young actors came to the casting.
Where can I find a casting for models?
casting.note: Also a form of the verb "cast": "casting a vote", "casting a shadow".

ex: My inbox is full of spam again today.
This email filter blocks most of the spam.
Don't click on links in spam emails.
How do I stop all this spam on my phone?
spam.note: Uncountable: some spam, a lot of spam (not "a spam").

ex: The island has unique flora and fauna.
Scientists came here to study the local flora.
The desert flora can live with very little water.
This park is famous for its rare mountain flora.

home run.note: A baseball word; "hit a home run" can also mean have a big success.

fast food.note: Uncountable: some fast food (not "a fast food").

ex: Thousands of fans came to watch the grand prix.
The grand prix starts on Sunday afternoon.
She finished second in the grand prix race.
Where can we watch the grand prix on TV?
grand prix.note: Usually a big car race; plural "grands prix". Also the top prize at a festival.

pop-up.note: Also "a pop-up shop": a store that is open only for a short time.

cross-country.note: Also "a cross-country trip": a trip across a whole country.

ex: Take the lift to the fifth floor.
Sorry, the lift is out of order today.
Where is the lift in this hotel?
The lift was full, so we took the stairs.
lift.note: Most often "lift" means raise: "Lift the box." The elevator sense is British; in the US say "elevator".

major.note: Most often "major" means big or important: "a major problem."

ex: I eat a sweet mango for breakfast every day.
Can I have a mango smoothie, please?
Mangoes grow well in hot countries.
Cut the mango into small pieces for the salad.

impact.note: Say "have an impact on": "Sleep has an impact on health."

security.note: Most often "security" means safety: "national security", "job security".

Yankee.note: Often part of a baseball team's name; for an American it is informal and can sound rude.

ex: My uncle is a recovering alcoholic now.
Her father was an alcoholic for many years.
This group helps alcoholics stop drinking.
An alcoholic needs support from family and friends.
alcoholic.note: Also an adjective: "alcoholic drinks" (drinks with alcohol).

ex: Plants take in carbon dioxide from the air.
Cars produce a lot of carbon dioxide.
Too much carbon dioxide is bad for the planet.
Carbon dioxide levels in the air keep rising.
dioxide.note: Almost always with another word: "carbon dioxide".

ex: My parents were hippies in the 1960s.
The hippie had long hair and flowers.
He drives an old hippie van with flowers.
Hippies sang songs about peace and love.

volleyball.note: The game is uncountable: "play volleyball". The ball is "a volleyball".

ex: The newspaper's editorial criticized the new city plan.
She writes editorials for a weekly magazine.
Did you read today's editorial in the paper?
The editorial asks the city for new bike lanes.
editorial.note: Also an adjective: "the editorial team" (the people who edit).

ex: We went surfing early in the morning.
Surfing is very popular in Australia.
Where can I rent a board for surfing?
The waves are perfect for surfing today.
surfing.note: Also "surfing the web": going from one website to the next.

racist.note: Most often "racist" is an adjective: "a racist joke".

ex: The printer needs a new ink cartridge.
Where can I buy black ink cartridges?
Change the water filter cartridge every three months.
This old game cartridge still works perfectly.
cartridge.note: Also a bullet in its case for a gun: "a rifle cartridge".

ex: She has a background in nursing and teaching.
People here come from very different backgrounds.
His background is in sales and marketing.
Can you tell me about your background?
background.note: Also the back part of a picture: "a photo with a blue background".

caramel.note: Uncountable as a food; "a caramel" is one candy.

ex: The monarch gave a speech on TV today.
Britain and Spain still have a monarch.
The young monarch ruled for fifty years.
The old monarch lived in this castle.
monarch.note: Also a kind of butterfly: "a monarch butterfly".

ex: Her grandparents survived the Holocaust as children.
We visited a museum about the Holocaust.
Students learn about the Holocaust in history class.
Many films tell true stories from the Holocaust.
holocaust.note: Usually capitalized with "the" when it means the Nazi genocide.

ex: Check the log to find the error.
The server keeps a log of all visits.
Can you send me the error log, please?
The app saves a new log every day.
log.note: Also a thick piece of a tree, and the verb "log in": "Log in with your password."

ex: That was a mega party last night.
The band had a mega hit this summer.
They built a mega mall near our house.
Our school concert was a mega success.

lemonade.note: In the US, lemonade is lemon juice, water, and sugar, usually not fizzy.

delta.note: Also the Greek letter Δ, which means "change" in math and science.

vacuum.note: Often means a vacuum cleaner, or to clean with one: "I vacuum the floor."

processor.note: Also "a food processor": a kitchen machine that cuts and mixes food.

ex: He is an intellectual who reads all the time.
Many intellectuals left the country after the war.
She was a leading intellectual of her time.
The cafe was full of artists and intellectuals.
intellectual.note: Most often "intellectual" is an adjective: "intellectual work".

ex: The killer in the movie was a psychopath.
A psychopath often feels no guilt or fear.
Don't call him a psychopath just because he's rude.
Is the main character in this book a psychopath?
A scorpion was hiding in my shoe this morning.
Some scorpions have a very dangerous sting.
Scorpions live in hot and dry places.
Check your boots for scorpions in the desert.
My phone needs an update again.
The new update fixed the bug in the app.
I will send you an update tomorrow morning.
Can you give me a quick update on the project?
update.note: Also a verb: "Please update the app."

ex: She won the lottery jackpot last year.
The jackpot is now ten million dollars.
Nobody won the jackpot this week.
The slot machine paid out the jackpot.
jackpot.note: Idiom: "hit the jackpot" means have great luck.

ex: The genocide killed millions of people.
The court called the killings genocide.
We must never forget the victims of genocide.
The two leaders are accused of genocide.
He got diarrhea after drinking the tap water.
Drink plenty of water if you have diarrhea.
This medicine can sometimes cause diarrhea.
Do you have anything for diarrhea, please?
